document.title: Afghanistan: [Excised] Describes Pakistan's Current Thinking
document.publisher: National Security Archive (GWU), Taliban File Update
document.note: [Confidential] DCM Alan Eastham meets a source who appears to be Iftikhar Murshed. They review concerns about bin Laden's fatwa, the six plus two process, a proposed Ulema meeting of Taliban and future Northern Alliance, border security, and outside players. Murshed says Pakistan had not provided arms and ammunition to the Taliban for three or four months, apparently the first Pakistani admission of arms supplies.

events.description: DCM met a Pakistani MFA official, raised bin Ladin fatwa and Six-Plus-Two
Six-Plus-Two meeting chaired by Brahimi
Mullah Rabbani told Aziz Khan he wants a Taliban ulema list
Rabbani regime burned down the Pakistani embassy in Kabul
Masood met Hekmatyar twice in Tehran
Hekmatyar returned from Iran to Mazar-i-Sharif
DCM Eastham met Pakistani MFA official, raising bin Ladin's fatwa and the Pakistani link, Six-Plus-Two, and ulema proposal.
UN Six-Plus-Two meeting chaired by Brahimi approved joint talking points for use with Afghan factions.
Mullah Rabbani told Aziz Khan he wants the Taliban to produce an ulema list.
Hekmatyar returned to Mazar-i-Sharif from Iran at Iranian urging (last week before March 9).
Northern leaders held meetings in Kulyab (Tajikistan) discussing major military operations.
Masood met Hekmatyar twice during his visit to Tehran and discussed military planning.
Mazar-i-Sharif meetings agreed Rabbani as president, Dostam vice president, Masood defense minister, Hekmatyar prime minister.
Northern factions held meetings in Mazar-i-Sharif discussing major military operations and a power-sharing arrangement.
Northern meetings in Kulyab, Tajikistan discussed major military operations.
Hekmatyar returned to Mazar-i-Sharif from Iran at Iranian urging.
Masood visited Tehran and met Hekmatyar twice.
Rabbani regime burned down the Pakistani Embassy in Kabul.
GOP held inter-agency meetings to find ways to apply leverage on the Taliban, concluding border control is best.
US Embassy Islamabad cable reporting Pakistani official's admission on arms-related supplies to the Taliban.

relationships.quote: STRONG PRESSURE FROM THE UN AND U.S. TO SUPPORT THE PROCESS ALMOST CERTAINLY HELPED PROVOKE THIS CHANGE OF HEART.

key_claims: A Pakistani MFA official claimed Pakistan has little leverage over the Taliban.

The official said no Pakistani government arms or ammunition crossed the border in the previous three or four months; the embassy calls this the first admission that Pakistan supplied arms-related items.
The Taliban load up fuel for their planes in Pakistan.
Pakistan considered controlling its roughly 40 jeepable border crossing points but noted provincial governments are corrupted by smuggling.
Iran was said to be pushing the North toward an offensive on Kunduz and persuaded Hekmatyar to return to Mazar-i-Sharif.
Bin Ladin's fatwa was linked to Pakistan because Fazlur Rahman Khalil of Harakat-ul-Ansar signed it.
